extracted.intended_audience: general public, media, policymakers, and advocacy groups concerned with Roma, Gypsy and Traveller rights
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing whether comedic material that references the Holocaust or persecution of Roma/Sinti is acceptable and how platforms and public institutions should respond. Includes considerations of harm, legitimisation, platform responsibility, and urgent removal versus regulatory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate removal of Jimmy Carr’s Holocaust ‘joke’
rubrics_metrics.description: “Immediate removal of Jimmy Carr’s Holocaust ‘joke’ — We write to you demanding the removal of the ‘joke’ about the Holocaust from Jimmy Carr’s ‘His Dark Materials’ currently on Netflix.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter demands immediate removal rather than waiting for legislative change; frames removal as the primary appropriate platform response to the segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mock the experiences of Roma and Sinti during the Holocaust
rubrics_metrics.description: “Hundreds of thousands of Roma and Sinti people suffered prejudice, slave labour, sterilisation and mass murder simply because of their identity – these are not experiences for mockery.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content creators should not treat historical atrocities or the suffering of persecuted groups as material for jokes; such topics are explicitly labelled inappropriate for comedic treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform approval and funding legitimises discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: “Netflix’s approval and funding of this material legitimises and perpetuates discrimination and racism.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms that commission, host, or fund material risk endorsing the harmful message; platform endorsement is a criterion for culpability and requires remedial action (e.g., removal, policy changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content that normalises or endorses racism risks enabling further abuses
rubrics_metrics.description: “Jimmy Carr’s ‘joke’ about the murder of Gypsy and Roma people in the Holocaust is offensive and disgusting. It normalises and endorses racism – and this is a step towards crimes against humanity and genocide.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should consider whether material normalises or endorses racist attitudes; if so, it's judged as escalating harm with potential real-world consequences beyond offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the real-life consequences for Gypsy, Roma and Traveller communities
rubrics_metrics.description: “Allowing this material to exist on Netflix will have real life consequences. Gypsy, Roma and Traveller communities continue to face systematic discrimination.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should weigh tangible harms to targeted communities (increased discrimination, stigma, safety risks) rather than treating content as purely rhetorical or abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act urgently instead of awaiting regulatory change
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Culture Secretary has also condemned Netflix... legislation will change to regulate media content... However, we urge Netflix to remove ‘His Dark Materials’ immediately, rather than awaiting legislative change.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When content causes acute harm, prompt voluntary action by platforms is expected; delay pending regulation is criticised as insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public officials and democratic duty to protect marginalised groups in public discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: “The duty of democratically elected representatives mindful of our own past, is to be a clarion voice for the fringe, for the dispossessed and those whom the privileged ridicule... Our duty as democrats is to acknowledge and value the worth of the Gypsy, Roma and Traveller community… and to raise them up, not put them down.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policymakers and public figures should evaluate and respond to harmful speech with a protective stance toward vulnerable groups, using public voice and policy influence to counter ridicule and marginalisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional responses: education and policing for race hate incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: “Racial hatred of this magnitude is intolerable in a civilised society. I hope that schools will reinforce the message that all people are of equal worth... and that police forces up and down the country will take appropriate measures to address such dangerous race hate incidents and crimes.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation includes whether the content warrants wider institutional responses (educational reinforcement, law enforcement action); harmful material may trigger cross-sector interventions beyond platform moderation.
